description: Readiness check examples (ticket 2.7): `npm run eval -- readiness` sends each approved spec to the real readiness check (prompt readiness-v1). The three workshop example specs must pass (verdict ready); each spec needing a login, a payment, an outside service, a server of its own or leaving a question open must fail (verdict not-ready) with a reason that names the problem (one of the example's keywords, any case).

examples.name: fitness tracker (example)
examples.spec:
# Run Log

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  home[Home] -->|add a run| add[Add a run]
  add -->|saves| runs[(Runs)]
  runs -->|weekly total and longest run| home
```

## What it does
A personal log of your runs. You add each run with its date, distance and time, and the home screen shows this week's total distance and your longest run so far.

## Screens
- Home: this week's total distance, your longest run and the list of runs, newest first.
- Add a run: date, distance in km and time in minutes, with a Save button.

## Data it keeps
- Runs: date, distance in km and time in minutes for each run.

examples.name: movie tracker (example)
examples.spec:
# Movie Watchlist

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  list[Watchlist] -->|add a film| add[Add a film]
  add -->|saves| films[(Films)]
  list -->|tick off and rate| films
  films -->|watched films| watched[Watched]
```

## What it does
A watchlist of films you want to see. You add a film with its title and year, tick it off once watched and give it 1 to 5 stars.

## Screens
- Watchlist: the films still to watch, each with a Watched button.
- Add a film: title and year, with a Save button.
- Watched: the films you have seen, with their stars, best rated first.

## Data it keeps
- Films: title, year, whether it was watched and its rating from 1 to 5 stars.

examples.name: nutrition calculator (example)
examples.spec:
# Calorie Counter

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  today[Today] -->|add a food| add[Add a food]
  add -->|saves| foods[(Foods eaten)]
  foods -->|daily total| today
  today -->|set goal| goal[Daily goal]
  goal -->|saves| settings[(Goal)]
```

## What it does
A daily calorie counter. You type in each food you eat with its calories, and the app adds them up for the day and compares the total with your daily goal.

## Screens
- Today: the foods eaten today, the total calories and how much is left of the goal.
- Add a food: the food's name and its calories, with an Add button.
- Daily goal: the number of calories you aim for each day.

## Data it keeps
- Foods eaten: name, calories and the day it was eaten.
- Goal: the daily calorie goal.

examples.name: habit tracker with personal accounts
examples.spec:
# Team Habit Tracker

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  signin[Sign in] -->|password| home[My habits]
  home -->|tick a habit| habits[(Habits)]
  habits -->|streaks| home
```

## What it does
Each colleague signs in with their own username and password and sees only their own habits. They tick off habits every day and see their streaks.

## Screens
- Sign in: username and password; new colleagues create an account here.
- My habits: today's habits to tick off and each habit's streak, visible only to the person signed in.

## Data it keeps
- Accounts: username and password of each colleague.
- Habits: name, days ticked off and the owner's account.

examples.name: bake sale shop with card payment
examples.spec:
# Bake Sale Shop

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  menu[Cakes] -->|add to basket| basket[Basket]
  basket -->|pay by card| checkout[Checkout]
  checkout -->|saves| orders[(Orders)]
```

## What it does
An online shop for our office bake sale. Colleagues choose cakes, put them in a basket and pay by credit card at checkout, so the money goes to charity.

## Screens
- Cakes: the cakes on sale with their prices.
- Basket: the chosen cakes and the total price.
- Checkout: card number, expiry date and a Pay button.

## Data it keeps
- Orders: the cakes ordered, the total paid and the time of the order.

examples.name: weather dashboard with a live forecast
examples.spec:
# Office Weather Board

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  board[Weather board] -->|fetch forecast| forecast[(Forecast)]
  board -->|add a city| cities[Cities]
  cities -->|saves| list[(City list)]
```

## What it does
A dashboard that shows today's live weather forecast for the cities of our offices, fetched every hour from a weather forecast API.

## Screens
- Weather board: the current temperature and today's forecast for each city, updated every hour.
- Cities: add or remove the cities shown.

## Data it keeps
- City list: the names of the cities shown.
- Forecast: the latest forecast fetched from the weather API for each city.

examples.name: plant reminders sent by email
examples.spec:
# Plant Care

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  plants[My plants] -->|add a plant| add[Add a plant]
  add -->|saves| list[(Plants)]
  list -->|due today| reminders[Reminders]
```

## What it does
A list of house plants with how often each needs water. Every morning the app sends me an email listing the plants to water that day.

## Screens
- My plants: each plant and when it was last watered.
- Add a plant: name and how many days between waterings.

## Data it keeps
- Plants: name, days between waterings and the date it was last watered.

examples.name: quiz with an undecided scoring rule
examples.spec:
# Coffee Quiz

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  start[Start] -->|play| question[Question]
  question -->|answer| question
  question -->|finished| result[Result]
  result -->|saves| scores[(Scores)]
```

## What it does
A quiz about our office's coffee machine for a team event. We still need to decide whether wrong answers cost points or not; to be decided with the team before the event.

## Screens
- Start: the quiz's title and a Play button.
- Question: one question at a time with four answers.
- Result: your score and the best scores so far.

## Data it keeps
- Scores: player's chosen nickname and score.
- Questions: to be decided: either the ten questions written by Sam or questions anyone can add.

examples.name: expense splitter with a server that runs at night
examples.spec:
# Trip Splitter

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  trip[Trip] -->|add an expense| add[Add an expense]
  add -->|saves| expenses[(Expenses)]
  expenses -->|balances| trip
```

## What it does
Splits the costs of a team trip. People add what they paid, and every night at midnight a server program recalculates who owes whom, even when nobody has the app open.

## Screens
- Trip: who paid what and the balances.
- Add an expense: who paid, what for and how much.

## Data it keeps
- Expenses: payer, description and amount.
- Balances: what each person owes, recalculated every night.
